tells.1: none; its quirks (dash bullets, 'Never miss a session again', 'watch your progress grow!', clunky renewal boilerplate) read like typical human-written store copy
tells.2: Invented-feeling specifics: the precise '312' count, a named testimonial ('Gwen Harper... back to hiking in four months'), and a new Premium feature, plus the awkward 'the bigger problem is X, more than Y' framing
tells.3: Over-flattened, neutral tone with tidy parallel bullets ('300+ video exercises. / Reminders. / Progress sharing.') that strip out any voice
tells.4: Generic polish and filler: 'guidance you can trust', 'keep your recovery moving', 'unlock more of what the app has to offer'
tells.5: Slightly forced casualness and stock momentum phrases ('bouncing back', 'keep you moving forward', 'get moving')

reason: Version 5 is clear and warm, and it reads naturally without inventing claims. Version 2's fabricated-seeming testimonial and stat are a credibility and compliance risk for a health app, and Version 4 is the most generically AI-polished.
